result: In 43 CFS trial entrants, CD3, CD4, CD8, activated and naive/memory T-cell percentages did not differ from controls, while NK cells and CD11b+ CD8 cells were higher; no immune measure changed with treatment or predicted response.
reason: Measures flow subset proportions, not CD8 exhaustion transcriptional/chromatin programmes; closest is the CD8 memory-subset shift in immune-mait, which it does not find.

result: In 11 CFS vs 11 sedentary controls, vagal (0.15-1.0 Hz) power was lower during each treadmill walking bout and one rest period, and fell further at rest after walking, with no differences in heart rate or VO2.
reason: Same HF-band vagal measure, adds exercise context and post-exertion decline; small sample.

result: Post-exercise MEP facilitation after isometric wrist-extensor fatigue was 126% of baseline in 12 CFS vs 218% in 18 controls and 155% in 10 depressed patients; post-exercise MEP depression was similar across groups.
reason: Different method (TMS vs fMRI) but same mechanism of reduced central motor-cortex response to fatiguing exercise; not specific, also seen in depression.

result: In 548 chronically fatigued patients, seroprevalence and GMTs to 13 viruses including EBV, HHV-6, CMV and Coxsackie B were not consistently different from controls, including in CFS, acute-onset and febrile subsets.
reason: Independent large cohort, same serology measure, same null result.

result: Women with CFS who reached VO2 max had lower VO2 max than controls (28.1 vs 32.1 mL/kg/min, P=0.05; n=10 vs 17), though 98% of predicted, with higher RPE at equal workloads.
reason: Same measure, same direction, small sample and borderline significance.

result: 21 women with CFS withstood a maximal treadmill test without a major exacerbation of fatigue or other symptoms.
reason: Reports no major post-test symptom exacerbation, opposite to prolonged post-CPET PEM; timing not measured and method not described.

result: Of 246 self-referred CFS patients followed 18 months, 3% reported complete recovery and 17% improvement; predictors were sense of control, less fatigue, shorter duration and fewer physical attributions.
reason: Independent prospective cohort, same outcome, low recovery consistent with the median 5%.

result: Calf 31P-MRS post-exercise PCr resynthesis Vmax was lower in 22 CFS than 15 sedentary controls (39.6 vs 53.8 mmol/L/min), and Vmax and resting Pi/PCr were unchanged 2 days after a maximal treadmill test (n=14).
reason: Same 31P-MRS muscle literature the finding covers (incl. slower ATP synthesis); adds a group-level oxidative capacity deficit vs sedentary controls, not pH.

result: Muscle oxidative capacity (PCr Vmax) and resting Pi/PCr did not change 2 days after a maximal treadmill test in 14 CFS patients.
reason: Measures muscle metabolism after exertion, not PEM symptom onset, duration or recovery.

result: In 10 healthy nurses, 5 days of night shift raised basal ACTH (12.9 vs 4.7 pmol/L), lowered cortisol (551 vs 871 nmol/L), blunted the integrated ACTH response to CRH and increased the cortisol response.
reason: Healthy shift workers, no ME/CFS patients; CRH challenge confounder model, not a test of the ACTH/glucocorticoid feedback finding.
